verdict: 4/10. In stills V1 already looks like Ifverse: the palette, black-head stickmen, letterbox, grain, window god-rays, and a well-planted script. As a video it can't ship. A pipeline bug (placeholder 2.5 s VO, every speaker NAR) put about 58 s of narration on top of itself, left every mouth shut, desynced every line-anchored cut and cut the runtime to 4:50. On top of that, the climax lies to the viewer: two clocks disagree, the robot passes through the barrier, and triumph music plays before anything is solved. The tournament (a third of the film) is lit flat and cold, and the characters move like posed paper dolls. Compared with the reference: our rims are half as thick, close-ups sit dead centre instead of on thirds, OTS shots show faces instead of the backs of heads, and the arena has no visible key light. V2 is a re-render with the bug fixed plus a focused clarity pass on Act 3. The script does not need rewriting.

conflicts_resolved.topic: Narration cuts vs runtime >= 5:30 (story: cut L065 and L076/L077; brief: 5:30-6:00)
conflicts_resolved.decision: Cut L065 and L076, keep L077, and keep L050 but move it onto S069.
conflicts_resolved.why: With real VO the edit is 345 s. Cutting L065 (~5.4 s) and L076 (~6 s) and shortening S092 (-1 s) removes ~12 s. The P0/P1 holds and inserts add ~17 s (S066/S067 +4, robot-stuck inserts +2.5, apology pauses +2, end title on black +2.5, S068 silent sweeps +2.5, climax flash cuts +1.5, S088 silent beat +1.5, S095 slow-mo +0.6), so V2 lands at ~350 s (5:50), inside the window. L064 'I told you that three weeks ago!' plus the S087 flashback already explain the realisation, so L065 is redundant. L077 is the emotional line, and L076 restates the premise the rule card already showed. Add a build guard: fail if the total is outside 330-360 s.

conflicts_resolved.topic: S001 hook: split into S001 + S001b CU (rhythm) vs keep one split-screen shot showing the equal outcome (story)
conflicts_resolved.decision: Story's content in a single shot, capped at 6 s.
conflicts_resolved.why: The first 6 s have to sell '1 hour = 10 hours'. One shot that pushes 1.0->1.15 and ends on the '=' wipe does that better than a cut to an Eli CU. If the retimed shot exceeds 6.0 s, add S001b (Eli smiling CU, CAM.push 1->1.1) as overflow, not as a design goal.

conflicts_resolved.topic: S026/S108 callback face: logic says make S026 'bewildered' to match S108; story says make S108 open on S026's wide-eyed shock face
conflicts_resolved.decision: Keep S026 as wide-eyed shock. S108 opens on the identical face and framing, then droops to deadpan on 'Oh my God'.
conflicts_resolved.why: The shock take is the more readable and funnier beat in Act 1. The callback works by repeating it, then subverting it. Both shots share headAt and h, placed on the right third (this also satisfies lighting's thirds rule).
The test sheet has 7 visible questions. VO L020 only says 'almost every answer was right', so 6/7 is consistent with what's on screen.
